reasoning_details.text: The user is asking for the conversion factor between workdays and work-hours. This is a simple factual question about the assumption I made earlier. In my assumptions, I stated "A workday is 8 hours of focused development effort". So I should return 8.

technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt Go modules with external Fabric repository references instead of vendored internal copies
Pin each externalized module to a specific tagged Fabric release to ensure reproducible builds

For modules that exist as 'modified copies' (gossip protoext, common utilities, configtxgen, configtxlator), evaluate whether SDK modifications should be upstreamed or reintroduced as a thin SDK-local adapter layer
For unmodified copies (cauthdsl, ccprovider, ledger portions), perform a straight externalization with import-path rewrites
Implement the chaincode go.mod honoring as a feature-flagged, opt-in workaround with clear deprecation comments, since U6 acknowledges it is short-lived
Preserve existing public SDK APIs; introduce internal adapter packages where needed to avoid breaking consumers
Update CI/CD pipelines (linters, unit tests, integration tests) to consume the new external modules
assumptions: A single senior Go developer is performing all work and is familiar with both Fabric core and Fabric Go SDK
A workday is 8 hours of focused development effort (excludes meetings, code reviews beyond self-review)
Upstream Fabric already has the required packages exposed and tagged as Go modules (or will be coordinated in parallel)
The SDK's existing test suite is comprehensive enough to validate the refactor; no new test cases for previously untested code paths are required
No new features are introduced; this is a pure refactoring/externalization effort plus one temporary workaround
Code review/merge cycle with maintainers is not included in the developer effort estimate
Ledger externalization (U4) is treated as the largest item because it spans core/ledger and has many transitive consumers within the SDK
Effort estimates for U1, U5, U7, U8 include time to reconcile SDK-specific modifications with upstream behavior
U6 implementation focuses on the chaincode packaging/build path only; documentation of its temporary nature is included

activities.activity_description: Inventory all eight user stories, survey the current internal/third_party copies in fabric-sdk-go, identify the Fabric upstream modules to depend on, decide on import-path mapping, and document the externalization strategy.

Remove the modified internal copy of gossip protoext utilities, reconcile SDK-specific modifications with upstream behavior, update all import paths in the SDK, and add the external Fabric module dependency.
Delete the third_party copy of common/cauthdsl, point the SDK to the upstream Fabric module, and update affected import paths.
Delete the third_party copy of core/common/ccprovider, point the SDK to the upstream Fabric module, and update affected import paths.
Delete the third_party copy of core/ledger used by the SDK, add the external Fabric ledger module dependency, and update all transitive import paths and consumer code.
Remove the modified internal copies of common utilities and core utilities, reconcile SDK modifications, and switch to the upstream Fabric modules with updated import paths.
Modify the chaincode packaging/build path to honor go.mod files present in a chaincode package as a temporary, short-lived workaround. Include deprecation comments and feature flag.

Remove the modified internal copy of configtxgen functions, reconcile SDK-specific changes with upstream, update import paths in pkg/fab/resource/configtx.go and related files, and depend on the external module.
Remove the modified internal copy of configtxlator functions, reconcile SDK-specific changes with upstream, update import paths, and depend on the external module.

Update go.mod and go.sum to reflect new external dependencies, remove replace directives where no longer needed, update CI scripts, linter configurations, and Makefile targets to handle the new module layout.

Run the full unit and integration test suites across the SDK, fix regressions caused by API differences between the SDK's internal copies and the external modules, and verify end-to-end scenarios for each externalized package.

Update README, CHANGELOG, migration notes, and developer docs to reflect the removal of internal/third_party copies, the new module dependencies, and the temporary nature of the chaincode go.mod workaround.
